content:
In this BUILT Insights we share the Advanced Technologies for Industry – ATI project.


ATI was created within the European Commission with the aim of carrying out systematic monitoring of technological trends and producing reliable, up-to-date data on advanced technologies. This is in order to properly support the implementation of policies and initiatives in line with the industrial policy approach that the European Union wants to implement to promote a competitive industry.


The ATI project and its platform therefore provide policy makers, industry representatives and academia, or other associations, such as BUILT CoLAB, with statistical data on: the creation and use of advanced technologies (including information on enabling conditions, such as skills, investment or entrepreneurship); analytical reports on technological trends, sectoral insights and products, analyses of policy measures and tools related to the adoption of advanced technologies; analyses of technological trends in competitive economies, such as the USA, China or Japan; and also access to technology centres and innovation centres in all EU countries.


ATI focuses on the advanced technologies that will enable and help industries to successfully manage a shift towards a low-carbon, knowledge-based economy. The following 16 advanced technologies have been identified:


Advanced Manufacturing Technology, Advanced Materials, Artificial Intelligence, Augmented and Virtual Reality, Big Data, Blockchain, Cloud Computing, Connectivity, Industrial Biotechnology, Internet of Things, Micro- and Nanoelectronics, Mobility, Nanotechnology, Photonics, Robotics, Security.


For more information about the project, visit the ATI website.
